mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during INDPRO contraction episodes compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes corporate earnings power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE and rising PAYEMS) above 62% for four consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and corporate costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS rising with participation > 62% for 4 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during episodes of sustained high labor force participation and rising employment (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which lifts corporate revenues and profit forecasts, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of sustained monthly retail sales growth above 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
